> Fetch a UniProt entry with its annotated modifications, digest it, and return every peptidoform with its fragment ions, plus a census of which annotations were applied.

Wire verb `peptidoform fragments` · Python [`pymzlib.peptidoform.fragments`][pymzlib.peptidoform.fragments]

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `accession` | `string` | required | — | — | A UniProtKB accession, e.g. P02768; fetched from rest.uniprot.org. The bridge checks only that it is not blank (the bindings upper-case it and check its shape first). UniProt's 400 or 404 becomes a usage error. |
| `protease` | `string` | `trypsin\|P` | — | `a key of mzLib's ProteaseDictionary` | mzLib protease name. The default "trypsin\|P" is the Keil rule (cleave after K/R EXCEPT before P); mzLib's plain "trypsin" cleaves before P too. The bracket/bar marks a PREVENTING residue, the reverse of MaxQuant's and Mascot's "Trypsin/P". |
| `dissociation` | `string` | `ETD` | — | `a mzLib DissociationType name, case-insensitive: HCD, CID, ETD, EThcD, ...` | Which fragment series to generate: HCD/CID give b and y; ETD gives c and zDot. |
| `terminus` | `string` | `Both` | — | `a mzLib FragmentationTerminus name, case-insensitive: Both, N, C` | Which fragment termini to generate; also passed to DigestionParams. |
| `no_modifications` (wire `--no-modifications`) | `flag` | `false` | — | — | Digest the bare sequence: UniProt's modifications are discarded but its signal-peptide and propeptide boundaries are kept (pyMzLib#8), so the backbone peptide list is unchanged and only the modified variants go away. A clean control. |
| `missed_cleavages` (wire `--missed-cleavages`) | `int` | `2` | cleavage sites | `>= 0` | Maximum missed cleavage sites per peptide. |
| `min_length` (wire `--min-length`) | `int` | `7` | residues | `>= 1` | Shortest peptide kept. The default silently drops shorter peptides (about a third of a histone digest); pass 1 for every peptide. |
| `max_length` (wire `--max-length`) | `int` | `0` | residues | `>= 0` | Longest peptide kept; 0 means unbounded. |
| `max_mods` (wire `--max-mods`) | `int` | `2` | modifications | `>= 0` | Maximum modifications per peptidoform (DigestionParams maxModsForPeptides). Isoforms grow combinatorially: histone H3.1 gives 49 bare tryptic peptides, 2,563 at 2 and 7,040 at 3. |
| `max_isoforms` (wire `--max-isoforms`) | `int` | `1024` | peptidoforms | `>= 1` | Cap on modification isoforms per peptide position (DigestionParams maxModificationIsoforms). mzLib truncates SILENTLY at the cap; peptides_at_isoform_cap reports it. |

### Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `accession` | `string` | — | never | The accession UniProt returned. |
| `name` | `string` | — | yes: the entry records no entry name | UniProt entry name, e.g. ALBU_HUMAN. |
| `full_name` | `string` | — | yes: the entry records no recommended name | Recommended protein name, e.g. Albumin. |
| `organism` | `string` | — | yes: the entry records no organism | Scientific name. |
| `sequence_length` | `int` | residues | never | Length of the full precursor sequence. |
| `modifications_applied` | `bool` | — | never | False under no-modifications. |
| `annotated_modification_sites` | `int` | residues | never | Distinct residue positions carrying at least one loaded modification. Not a modification count: K9me1/me2/me3/ac are four modifications at one site. |
| `annotated_modifications_loaded` | `int` | modifications | never | Modifications mzLib loaded onto the protein (summed over sites). Counted from the annotated entry, so unchanged by no-modifications. |
| `uniprot_annotated_features` | `int` | features | never | Modification-like features in the XML: modified residue, glycosylation site, lipid moiety-binding region and cross-link. |
| `unresolved_modifications` | `string[]` | — | never | Modification names the entry annotates that could not be resolved against UniProt's ptmlist, sorted. These are dropped silently by mzLib otherwise. |
| `uniprot_features_by_type` | `object[]` | — | never | {type, count, loaded} per feature type, sorted by type. loaded is true only for 'modified residue' and 'lipid moiety-binding region': mzLib drops the others on feature TYPE alone, before any mass lookup. |
| `protease` | `string` | — | never | The protease used. |
| `dissociation` | `string` | — | never | DissociationType name used. |
| `terminus` | `string` | — | never | FragmentationTerminus name used. |
| `max_modifications` | `int` | modifications | never | max-mods, echoed. |
| `max_modification_isoforms` | `int` | peptidoforms | never | max-isoforms, echoed. |
| `peptides_at_isoform_cap` | `int` | peptide positions | never | Peptide positions (start, end) whose distinct peptidoforms reached max-isoforms. Non-zero means the list is TRUNCATED. |
| `peptide_count` | `int` | peptidoforms | never | Entries in peptides. |
| `peptides` | `object[]` | — | never | One entry per distinct peptidoform (start, end, full sequence), in digestion order; fields under result.columns. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `base_sequence` | `string` | — | never | Bare residues. |
| `full_sequence` | `string` | — | never | mzLib full sequence with modifications inline, e.g. ...K[UniProt:N6-succinyllysine on K]. |
| `monoisotopic_mass` | `float` | Da | never | Neutral monoisotopic mass, modifications included. |
| `length` | `int` | residues | never | Peptide length. |
| `one_based_start` | `int` | — | never | First residue's position in the protein, 1-based. |
| `one_based_end` | `int` | — | never | Last residue's position in the protein, 1-based, inclusive. |
| `missed_cleavages` | `int` | cleavage sites | never | Missed cleavage sites spanned. |
| `modification_count` | `int` | modifications | never | Entries in modifications. |
| `fixed_charges` | `int` | charge | never | Formal charges the INTACT peptide carries before protonation (e.g. trimethyllysine's quaternary ammonium), recovered from each modification's formula-vs-recorded mass deficit in whole electrons. m/z at charge z is (monoisotopic_mass + (z - fixed_charges) * 1.00727646677) / z. Does NOT apply to fragments. |
| `modifications` | `object[]` | — | never | {one_based_residue, terminus, id, mass, formal_charge} per modification: one_based_residue is 1-based within the PEPTIDE and null for a terminal modification, which sets terminus 'N' or 'C' instead (terminus is null for a residue modification); id is mzLib's IdWithMotif; mass is its monoisotopic mass in Da (null only if the modification defines none); formal_charge in elementary charges. |
| `fragments` | `object[]` | — | never | {product_type, fragment_number, neutral_mass, neutral_loss, residue_position} per ion: product_type e.g. b, y, c, zDot; fragment_number the position in its series; neutral_mass the monoisotopic NEUTRAL mass in Da (not an m/z; no proton added); neutral_loss in Da (0 when none); residue_position 1-based within the peptide. |

### Errors

| Kind | pyMzLib raises | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | accession missing or blank; UniProt answers 400 or 404 (no such entry); the entry holds no protein sequence; protease not in ProteaseDictionary; dissociation or terminus not an enum name; an integer option that is not an integer |
| `service_unavailable` | [`ServiceUnavailableError`][pymzlib.ServiceUnavailableError] | UniProt unreachable by the bridge's own classification: a timeout (HttpClient 100 s), a socket or TLS failure, a request that never got a response, an HTTP 408, 429 or 5xx, or a body cut off in transit |
| `correctness` | [`BridgeError`][pymzlib.BridgeError] | any other UniProt status (e.g. 403); UniProt's ptmlist.txt or PSI-MOD.obo.xml missing from the bridge payload (FileNotFoundException: every protein would otherwise look unmodified or carry wrong charges); mzLib failing to parse the entry or to digest it |

### Caveats

- UniProt annotates more than mzLib applies: only 'modified residue' and 'lipid moiety-binding region' features load. Serum albumin: 14 of 38 annotated features applied, the 24 glycosylation-site features dropped on type (mzLib#1112). Read uniprot_features_by_type and unresolved_modifications before trusting a modification count.
- max-isoforms truncates silently in mzLib (histone H3.1 at four modifications loses about 30% of peptidoforms at 1024). Check peptides_at_isoform_cap before treating the list as exhaustive.
- Duplicate peptidoforms that mzLib's Digest emits where a chain boundary meets the initiator-Met cleavage site (mzLib#1108, open) are collapsed by the bridge on (start, end, full sequence).
- Fragment masses are neutral. Converting one to m/z needs the fixed charge within that fragment's span, which the wire does not report; fixed_charges is whole-peptide only.
- ETD's zDot ions are suppressed N-terminal to proline while the complementary c ions are not, leaving about 4% of the c series unobservable (mzLib#1110).
- Needs the network: UniProt is queried on every call.

### Example

```python
digest = pymzlib.peptidoform.fragments('P02768', max_modifications=1)
```

Recorded from the live bridge as [`peptidoform_P02768_small.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib/blob/main/pkg/python/tests/fixtures/peptidoform_P02768_small.json). The doctests in the API reference replay these recordings in CI.

    - Integer options are not range-checked by the bridge (negative min-length, max-isoforms 0); the bindings check them. Enum.TryParse also accepts numeric strings, so --dissociation 3 or --terminus 7 pass as undefined members. Behaviour of mzLib on such values is unverified.
